description: Gemini CLI agent integration, built in to the application.
configuration.title: Gemini
configuration.approval.allowAutoEdit: Offer the Auto Edit approval mode, which applies the agent's file edits without asking. When off, the mode is hidden and the Gemini CLI asks before every tool in it.
configuration.approval.allowYolo: Offer the YOLO approval mode, which runs every tool, including shell commands, without asking. When off, the mode is hidden and the Gemini CLI asks before every tool in it.
configuration.tools.allowShell: Let the agent run shell commands. Each command still asks first unless YOLO mode is on. When off, the Gemini CLI removes its shell tool.
command.appearance: Make It Yours: Theme, Font and Icons
walkthrough.look.title: Make it yours
walkthrough.look.description:
Pick a theme, a code font and file icons. Each choice applies at once.
[Choose a Look](command:gemini.appearance)
configuration.notifications.enabled: Show a system notification when an agent finishes or needs your permission while GeminiCode is in the background, and show how many agents are waiting on the Dock icon.
configuration.cli.checkForUpdates: Once a day, check the npm registry for a newer Gemini CLI and offer to install it. Nothing is installed without your click. No check is made when `#gemini.cli.version#` or `#gemini.cliPath#` is set.
configuration.app.checkForUpdates: Every few hours, check the GeminiCode download page for a newer GeminiCode and say so. GeminiCode downloads nothing itself; the notice links to the page.
configuration.agents.worktreeSetup: A shell command run in each new agent branch's folder before the agent starts, such as `npm ci && cp "$GEMINI_SOURCE_REPOSITORY/.env" .`. `GEMINI_SOURCE_REPOSITORY` is the repository the branch came from. When empty, the repository's own `.gemini/worktree-setup.sh` runs if it has one. Runs only in trusted workspaces.
configuration.projects.enabled: Projects: a project chat whose coordinator splits work into threads, each an agent on a new branch in its own worktree, shown as cards you can open, merge back or undo. The coordinator runs on a Flash model in an empty folder of its own and never edits files itself; you finish each thread's work in that thread. Start one with **New Project** in the Agents list.
configuration.agents.allWorkspaceFolders: Let every agent read and edit all folders of a multi-root window, not only the folder it works in. Off, an agent keeps to its own folder, and a project's coordinator to its own empty folder. Restarts the agent.
configuration.agents.ownBranch: Start every new agent in a Git repository on its own branch, in its own folder under `~/.geminicode/worktrees`, so agents working side by side never edit the same files. **Merge Back** on the agent brings its work into your branch. Off: agents work in the workspace folder, and **New Agent on Its Own Branch** does this for one agent.
configuration.chat.followAgent: Follow the agent: as it works, open each file it reads, and each file it edits once the edit is written, at the line it is on. Focus stays in the chat. Toggle it in the + menu of a chat's composer; new chats start the way you left it.
configuration.chat.reactions.enabled: React to Gemini's replies with an emoji. 👍 goes ahead, 👎 stops and asks what to change, ❓ asks for a simpler explanation, ❤️ is a thanks that sends nothing, and Gemini reads any other emoji as intent. Turn it off to hide the reaction button and chips.
configuration.chat.reactions.agentReacti: Let Gemini react to your messages with an emoji when it has something to add, such as good news. Most messages get none. Costs about 50 tokens per session.
configuration.chat.reactions.meanings: What an emoji reaction asks Gemini to do, by emoji, such as `{ "🚀": "Go ahead, then commit with a short message." }`. An entry changes one of the built-in meanings (👍 👎 ❓ ❤️) or adds one; the built-ins are never removed. Set it in a workspace's settings to share it with the team. Each meaning is at most 500 characters.
configuration.chat.foldFinishedWork: Fold each finished turn's thoughts and steps under one line, such as "Worked for 3m 12s · read 14 files, ran 9 commands", with the files it changed and any step that failed kept in sight. Click the line to see every step. Turn it off to show every step as it happened.
configuration.chat.spellCheck: Underline misspelled words in the chat and Agent Home composers, using your system's spell checker and languages. Right-click a word for suggestions.
configuration.browser.enabled: Let agents open and use a page in the GeminiCode browser, to check the web app they are working on: read it, click, type and take screenshots. Each agent gets its own tab, marked "Gemini is using this page". Applies to agents started afterwards.
configuration.browser.allowOtherSites: Let agents open sites other than this machine's (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, files), after asking you once per site. When off, agents can only open local pages.
configuration.browser.allowedOrigins: The only sites agents may open in the GeminiCode browser, such as `http://localhost:3000`, `http://localhost:*` (any port), `https://qa.example.com` or `https://*.example.com`; `*` allows all. Empty allows every site, as the other browser settings decide. You can still open any site yourself, but agents can't use a page on a site that isn't listed.
configuration.browser.keepSignIns: Keep the cookies and storage of agents' browser pages between sessions, separately for each workspace, so agents stay signed in to the sites they use, such as a QA environment. Agents' pages never share your own pages' storage: in remote and untrusted windows, or when `workbench.browser.dataStorage` keeps your pages' data per workspace, they stay in memory. Off: agents' pages forget everything when the agent closes.
configuration.index.enabled: Keep an index of the code in each folder agents work in, with the documentation you attach, and give agents tools to search it (`code_search`, `find_symbol`, `related_files`, `repo_map`, `docs_search`), so they find code in one step instead of searching file by file. The index stays on this machine, in `~/.geminicode/index`, and is built in a separate process at low priority. Applies to agents started afterwards.
configuration.index.buildOn: When a folder's index is first built. After that it is kept up to date as files change, whichever you pick.
configuration.index.buildOn.agentStart: When an agent first starts in the folder.
configuration.index.buildOn.workspaceOpe: When the window opens, for each folder in it.
configuration.index.buildOn.manual: Only when you choose Index Now on the Index page.
configuration.index.exclude: Files and folders to leave out of the index, in `.gitignore` syntax, such as `fixtures/` or `**/*.snap`. Files git ignores, `.geminiignore` entries, secret files such as `.env`, binaries and lock files are always left out.
configuration.index.include: Files to index even though they would be left out, in `.gitignore` syntax, such as `src/generated/**` or `docs/large-spec.md`: generated or minified code, lock files, files larger than `gemini.index.maxFileSizeKb` (up to 16 MB), and `.geminiignore` or `gemini.index.exclude` entries. Secret files such as `.env` and files with binary content are never indexed. **Index Anyway** on the Index page adds entries here.
configuration.index.maxFileSizeKb: Files larger than this, in KB, are left out of the index.
configuration.docs.enabled: Let you attach documentation from the web to a folder's index, for agents to search with `docs_search`. Pages are fetched from this machine, through its network settings.
configuration.docs.allowedDomains: The only sites documentation may be fetched from, such as `react.dev` or `*.example.com`. Empty allows every site.
configuration.docs.refresh: How often attached documentation is fetched again. A page that hasn't changed costs one small request.
configuration.agent.startEarly: Start the Gemini CLI a few seconds after GeminiCode opens, once you have signed in, so the first prompt does not wait for it. It uses about 230 MB of memory before the first chat.
configuration.home.openOnStartup: Open Home, the dashboard with your agents, Jira tickets, merge requests and checks, in front of your restored tabs every time GeminiCode starts. Turn it off to see Home only when no tab is open in Agents mode, or from the Agents pane.
configuration.team.openMergeRequestsIn: Where a merge request opens when you click it on Home, in the merge request panel or in the team flows.
configuration.team.openMergeRequestsIn.g: GeminiCode's browser, in a tab beside your work.
configuration.keepAwake: Keep the Mac from sleeping while any agent is working, so a long task is not paused when you step away. The display can still sleep. Ends as soon as no agent is working.
configuration.tools.denyEnvironmentComma: Refuse the shell commands that print the environment (`env`, `printenv`, and `set` or `export` alone), which would show an agent any token a server passes through it. On by default.
configuration.mcp.allowedServers: The only MCP servers agents may use, besides GeminiCode's own (team tools, projects, browser). Empty, the default, leaves it to the CLI's `mcp.allowed` setting, with GeminiCode's own servers always added; a name here outranks any repository's settings file.
configuration.team.runTeamServers: Run the tools' own MCP servers for the team tools' calls: the team's Jira and GitLab servers (mcp-atlassian, gitlab-mcp) and SonarSource's SonarQube server in Docker at pinned versions with your keychain tokens, and Snyk's server from your Snyk CLI. Jira's and GitLab's start when an agent's session opens, the others on their first call, and each stops when idle; while one is still starting, calls go to the tool directly. Without Docker, Jira, GitLab and SonarQube are called directly. With the SonarQube server, Checks also analyses the branch's changed files on this Mac. **Take Over Both Servers** in Connections turns this on.
configuration.pilot.record: For the pilot: count launches, waits before the first prompt, permission cards, Undo and Rewind, team tool errors and links that leave the app, with times and no text, in GeminiCode's own storage. **Gemini: Export Pilot Data** writes them with the audit log to `~/geminicode-pilot/`. Nothing is sent anywhere.
configuration.developer.showTools: Show GeminiCode's developer tools in the Command Palette: Run Benchmark, Record or Stop Performance Trace, Export Pilot Data, Show Status Menu, New Skill, and installing a Gemini CLI version. They still run from their buttons and links when this is off.
configuration.usageMeter.enabled: Show today's Gemini quota use in the Gemini status bar item's tooltip and in the chat's Usage and quota popover, and the percentage in the bar once a model passes 80%. Reads it every 10 minutes at most, and when the popover opens unless it was read in the last minute, with the sign-in the Gemini CLI saved. Google sign-in only.
configuration.inlineEdit.enabled: Inline edit (`⌘I` on a selection) and **Write Commit Message with Gemini**. Both send the selected code or the diff straight to a fast Gemini model, using the sign-in the Gemini CLI saved, without starting an agent.
configuration.inlineEdit.model: The model inline edit and commit messages use. `latestFlash` (the default) is the newest Flash model the installed Gemini CLI knows, or the previous one if your account can't use it yet, which keeps them to a second or two. `sameAsChat` uses the model last picked in chat, and Flash when that is Auto. Or enter a model name, such as `gemini-2.5-pro`.
configuration.cli.version: The version of GeminiCode's own copy of the Gemini CLI to run, such as `0.62.0`. When empty, the newest copy is used, installed or bundled with GeminiCode. Ignored when `#gemini.cliPath#` is set.
configuration.cliPath: Path to the Gemini CLI. Either a `gemini` executable or the CLI's JavaScript entry point (run with the application's bundled Node). When empty, GeminiCode's own copy is used (see `#gemini.cli.version#`): one installed from GeminiCode, the one bundled with it, or else `gemini` on `PATH`.

configuration.projectId: Google Cloud project ID the agent bills to, passed to the CLI as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`. Use the project ID, not the project number. A workspace value wins over a user value; when neither is set, the organisation default and then the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID` environment variables are used.

configuration.chat.runCommands: Run on shell commands in a reply (bash, zsh, sh, console, PowerShell): the command runs in the agent's own terminal, in its folder. Commands that delete or throw away work, force-push, run as root, run a download, write a disk or write outside the folder ask first, as do blocks of several commands.
configuration.chat.runCommands.askWhenRi: Run at once, and ask first for risky commands.
configuration.chat.runCommands.off: No Run button: replies' commands can only be copied.
